summary: Six criminal cases were filed inside the Fairbanks area during Tuesday — five at the Fairbanks courthouse and one at Delta Junction — on charges of theft, drunk driving, criminal trespass and reckless endangerment. None carries a felony count, and the Delta Junction case was dismissed by the court on the day it was filed. Alaska State Troopers arrested a woman at the Fairbanks trooper post on a warrant from a 2023 Nenana theft case in which she was convicted in January 2024, and reported seizing suspected drugs from inmates at Fairbanks Correctional Center. Earlier, troopers arrested a driver on a drunk-driving charge at North Pole after a vehicle left Badger Road and went into the trees. The Alaska Court System's weekly report of closed criminal cases, updated for the first time in a week, records a week of Interior outcomes: convictions for Steven Allen Judd on two counts of violating a domestic violence protective order, for Jordan Samuel Carlo on unlawful contact, and for drunk driving, reckless driving and a license-limit offense; dismissals of a repeat indecent exposure charge, two drunk-driving counts, two thefts and a four-year-old assault charge; and directed verdicts of acquittal on both counts of a Nenana case. A Fairbanks grand jury has indicted Nicholas John Pederson, 51, on a felony drunk-driving charge and the case has moved to the Superior Court. The weekly charges report covers Nov. 3 to Nov. 9 and lists 44 cases filed inside the Fairbanks area; it was last run on Monday night, so none of Tuesday's six filings appears in it.

entries.title: Warrant arrest: Trista Jennings
body: Trista Jennings, 42, of Anderson, was arrested on an outstanding warrant after walking into the Alaska State Troopers post at 1979 Peger Road in Fairbanks on Nov. 10 at about 9:20 a.m. to surrender herself. Troopers say she was contacted in the front lobby, taken into custody without incident and transported to Fairbanks Correctional Center.

The warrant is from case 4NE-23-00023CR at the Nenana court, in which she was convicted in January 2024 on one count of theft in the first degree — taking property worth $25,000 or more — after a guilty plea. Two further felony counts were dismissed by the prosecution. A restitution judgment of $141,859.17 was entered in February 2024.

The court reopened the case in February 2025 on a petition to revoke her probation and issued process on Feb. 25, 2025. The docket records the warrant served on Nov. 10, 2026. A petition to revoke probation is an allegation that a condition was broken and is not itself a conviction.

entries.title: Suspected drugs seized from inmates at Fairbanks Correctional Center
body: Correctional officers at Fairbanks Correctional Center found suspected contraband during a search on Nov. 10 at about 3:59 p.m., and Alaska State Troopers were called to the jail.

Troopers say officers located a white powdery substance, a white crystalline substance, Suboxone and marijuana concentrates in the possession of inmates, that the contraband was seized and that the investigation is continuing. No one has been named and no charge has been filed.

entries.title: DUI charge: Jason Ray Simcox
body: Jason Ray Simcox is charged with driving under the influence of alcohol or a drug — operating a vehicle while impaired — a Class A misdemeanor. The offense is recorded at North Pole on Nov. 10.
The charge was filed by complaint at the Fairbanks courthouse on Nov. 10 and conditions of release were entered the same day. Case 4FA-26-02264CR; arraignment Nov. 17 at 8:30 a.m.

entries.title: Theft charge: Bronson Fabron Dubois
body: Bronson Fabron Dubois is charged with theft in the third degree — taking property worth between $250 and $749 — a Class A misdemeanor. The offense is recorded at Fairbanks on Oct. 21.

entries.title: Reckless endangerment charge filed and dismissed: Kaden Ray Dawe
body: Kaden Ray Dawe was charged with reckless endangerment — recklessly creating a substantial risk of serious injury to another person — a Class A misdemeanor. The offense is recorded at Delta Junction on Oct. 20.

The charge was filed at the Delta Junction court on Nov. 10, he was arraigned at 1:30 p.m. the same day, and the docket records a court dismissal that day. A hearing set for Dec. 15 was vacated. Case 4DJ-26-00071CR. A dismissal is not a conviction and not a finding against him.

entries.title: DUI arrest at North Pole
body: A driver was arrested on a charge of driving under the influence — operating a vehicle while impaired by alcohol — after a vehicle drove off the roadway into the trees near Badger Road and Lincolnwood Drive in North Pole on Nov. 10 at about 1:06 a.m.

Alaska State Troopers say the investigation determined the driver had been driving under the influence of alcohol, that a breath test registered 0.181, and that the driver was taken to Fairbanks Correctional Center. Troopers have not released a name.

entries.title: Felony DUI indictment: Nicholas John Pederson
body: Nicholas John Pederson, 51, of Fairbanks, has been indicted by a Fairbanks grand jury on one count of felony driving under the influence with two or more prior convictions — drunk driving by someone convicted twice before within ten years. It is a Class C felony, punishable by up to five years.

Troopers say they responded on Oct. 24 to a vehicle collision on Chena Pump Road in Fairbanks, that the driver was arrested, and that a breath sample taken at the Peger Road post read 0.272. The offense is dated Oct. 25 on the court file.

Case 4FA-26-02159CR. The grand jury returned the indictment on Nov. 3 and the case was transferred to the Superior Court. Arraignment there is Nov. 18, with an omnibus hearing Dec. 10 and a trial week beginning Jan. 4, 2027.

entries.title: Motion filed in Cedar Sarten case ahead of sentencing
body: A motion for a representation hearing was filed on Nov. 9 on behalf of Cedar Mae Sarten, who was convicted by a Fairbanks jury in May of murder in the first degree in the killing of her five-year-old son.
A status hearing was held Nov. 6 and a transport order was entered the same day. Sentencing before Judge Bennett remains set for Jan. 29, 2027.
Case 4FA-24-02118CR.
